1.d4 Nf6 2.c4 d6 3.Nc3 e5 4.Nf3.strategy: The principal move: it develops with an attack on e5, which Black has to support at once, and keeps the choice between holding the tension and exchanging on e5. White keeps a healthy lead in space without committing the pawns.
1.d4 Nf6 2.c4 d6 3.Nc3 e5 4.Nf3.name: Old Indian Defence: Two Knights Variation

1.d4 Nf6 2.c4 d6 3.Nc3 e5 4.e3.strategy: Supports d4 with a pawn and frees the bishop instead of facing the tension on e5. It is solid but passive: Black gets time to finish development and White gives up the chance of an active centre.

1.d4 Nf6 2.c4 d6 3.Nc3 e5 4.e3 Nbd7.strategy: Defends e5 with a developing move and keeps the structure healthy. Against the quiet set-up Black needs nothing special: development and a firm hold on the centre are enough for an easy game.
